minutes.headline: Task force heard unions and department heads describe pay gaps and staff losses; it took no votes except adjourning.
minutes.summary: After debating whether two Zoom links on the agenda violated the open meeting law, the task force continued with no substantive votes. It heard from the teachers, police, fire, DPW and school secretaries about pay, retention and staffing, then discussed future meeting dates, a split tax rate presentation and a contract calendar. It adjourned on a motion.

attendees.role: town official (called the unofficial conary of the budget task force)

public_comment.topic: The chair asked for public comments; none were offered.

budget_items.what_was_said: The union president reviewed 15 years of teacher raises, including years of no increase, and compared them to inflation.
The contract manager compared cola raises since 2019 to the Social Security cola.
Mr pasos recalled a past contract round costing the town over three years.
The fire union president said the town invested in paramedic training and equipment under a five-year staffing plan.
A secretary representative said the highest paid secretary earns under a stated amount and the step range is narrow.
A member said BCBA hires offset out-of-district placement costs, which are among the largest and most surprising items.
A member said the new waste contract came in under expectations for three years, and suggested a reserve fund for carts when pay-as-you-throw ends.

decisions.decision: The task force chose to continue the meeting despite the two-Zoom-link concern, taking no substantive votes.
Administration to be asked for a schedule of when each town and school contract expires.
A meeting is to be held on the 23rd with the split tax rate presentation; Community Preservation Act to be paired with it later.

what_happened.line: The task force took no votes other than a motion to adjourn.
It chose to continue the meeting after a debate over whether two Zoom links on the agenda raised an open meeting law problem.
Teachers, police, fire, DPW and school secretaries described pay, retention and staffing, with the teachers' presentation the longest.
The task force decided to ask the administration for a schedule of when each town and school contract expires.
A meeting is set for the 23rd on a split tax rate, with the Community Preservation Act to be paired with it later.

why_it_matters: The task force is gathering what pay and staffing pressures look like by department before any figure goes to a town vote, so the contract-expiry schedule and the split tax rate session are where a resident's tax bill and town services come in.
The Zoom-link question touches how residents may attend and be heard at a public meeting.
